description: A two-operator cross-FM voice with a filter and a delay, built to make noise as readily as it makes tones

params.text: Sets the delay time, one millisecond at the far left and 5 seconds at the far right
Sets how much of the delay output is fed back into it, none at the far left and 0.95 at the far right
Sets the balance between the dry voice and the delayed signal
Sets the modulation depth applied to the first operator, 0.1 to 5; higher settings make a brighter and more crowded tone
Sets the modulation depth applied to the second operator, 0.1 to 5
Sets the first operator's frequency as a multiple of its pitch, 0.1 to 15; whole numbers give harmonic tones and anything between gives bell-like ones
Sets the second operator's frequency as a multiple of its pitch, 0.1 to 15
Sets the filter resonance, a wide peak at the far left and a sharp one at the far right
Sets the first operator's pitch, 1Hz to 1000Hz
Sets the second operator's pitch, 1Hz to 1000Hz
Sets the filter cutoff, 20Hz at the far left and 12000Hz at the far right
Chooses how the two operators are wired together: pure has the second modulating the first, wide runs them in parallel, and chaos has each modulating the other
Shifts the voice by an octave: sub drops it, bypass leaves it, and upper raises it
Chooses the filter: lp passes below the cutoff, bp passes around it and hp passes above it

inputs.text: Adds to the delay mix knob
Adds to the output gain knob
Adds to the first operator's frequency knob
Adds to the first operator's ratio knob
Adds to the first operator's index knob
Adds to the second operator's frequency knob
Adds to the second operator's ratio knob
Adds to the second operator's index knob
Adds to the delay time knob
Adds to the filter cutoff knob

notes: the module makes its own sound and takes no audio in; it needs no gate or trigger and starts sounding as soon as it is placed
the controls for the second operator are the ones printed with a line under the label
